original: It turns out that the most generous funder of white supremacist groups in the United States was likely the Southern Poverty Law Center. At least that's what the Department of Justice's superseding indictment against the SPLC alleges. The organization secretly paid informants to engage in the active promotion and funding of racist groups while denouncing and "fighting" the very same groups in public. The SPLC purportedly created fictitious entities to hide funding from their donors.
rewrite: Indeed, the SPLC, the most generous funder of white supremacist organizations in the U.S., appears to have been the target of allegations from the Department of Justice in its superseding indictment. The DOJ claims that the SPLC covertly funded and promoted racist groups through informants, while publicly denouncing them Additionally, the SPLC allegedly established fake entities to obscure its donors' contributions.

original: Way back there in the 1700s and the 1800s, the British conquered a big chunk of the world thanks to their navy, which was crewed by whip-scarred, toothless, unwilling sailors with untreated syphilis. That's who you want to fight your wars. No one fights like mistreated men living on a diet of garbage, the lash and below-decks rape.
rewrite: Way back in the 1700s and 1800s, the British secured vast territories through their formidable navy, which was manned by sailors who were whipped, toothless, and unwilling, suffering from untreated syphilis. These were the men you wanted to face in battle. No one fights like mistreated men, subsisting on meager rations of garbage, beaten by the lash, and subjected to rape below decks.

original: I was working at a medium-sized city newspaper on Sept. 11, 2001. No one had stormed the Capitol yet, there had been no George Floyd riots, we hadn't started the war we were going to lose in Afghanistan, and ICE hadn't killed anyone in the street.
rewrite: I was employed at a mid-sized city newspaper on September 11, 2001. No one had stormed the Capitol yet, there were no George Floyd protests, we hadn't initiated the war we were destined to lose in Afghanistan, and ICE had not yet killed anyone on the streets.

original: After I first started writing a column, in the fall of 2002, it wasn't long before I heard regularly from those who brandished God as a weapon in opposing LGBTQ rights. This was not surprising. Back then, I was on staff at The Plain Dealer in Cleveland, and I was long familiar with the bigotry in my home state. Most of the hate mail came from strangers, but I got my share of lectures from blood relatives, too. Few things anger right-wing Christians more than a family member insisting she's acquainted with a different version of God.
rewrite: After I began writing a column in the fall of 2002, it wasn't long before I received regular correspondence from individuals who used God as a tool to oppose LGBTQ rights. This was unsurprising. At the time, I was employed at The Plain Dealer in Cleveland, and I was already well-acquainted with the bigotry in my home state. Most of the hate mail came from anonymous sources, but I also received lectures from family members. Few things infuriate right-wing Christians more than a family member who claims to know a different version of God.

original: "We didn't celebrate the Fourth of July," he told me. "For us, it was the day Vicksburg fell." Vicksburg, Mississippi, fell to Union troops on July 4, 1863. The Confederates surrendered, as was their habit. Long memories still mourn the Lost Cause of Black backs whipped bloody.
rewrite: "We didn't celebrate the Fourth of July," he informed me. "For us, it was the day Vicksburg fell." Vicksburg, Mississippi, capitulated to Union forces on July 4, 1863. The Confederates surrendered, as they often did. Deep-seated memories still mourn the Lost Cause of black backs who were beaten with cruel whips.
